stem: If scrape_interval isn't set anywhere in prometheus.yml, how often does Prometheus scrape targets?

options.note: Right. The built-in global default for scrape_interval is 1m.
15s is common in examples, including the getting-started guide, but it isn't the built-in default.
10s is the default scrape_timeout, not the interval.
No scrape setting defaults to 5 minutes.

explanation: In the global configuration, scrape_interval defaults to 1m, scrape_timeout to 10s, and evaluation_interval to 1m.
hint: Examples often override it. What's the value when nobody does?

stem: Which pairs correctly match a global setting with its built-in default? Select all that apply.

options.note: Right. The default scrape timeout is 10 seconds.
Right. Rules are evaluated every minute by default.
The default scrape_interval is 1m.
The default timeout is 10s, and it can't exceed the scrape interval.

explanation: Defaults: scrape_interval 1m, scrape_timeout 10s (never greater than the interval), evaluation_interval 1m.
hint: The timeout is the short one.

stem: Which setting belongs in a command-line flag rather than in prometheus.yml?

options.text: How long to retain data on disk
options.note: Right. Storage retention is an immutable system parameter set by flags such as --storage.tsdb.retention.time.

options.text: The list of targets for a job
options.note: Scrape jobs and targets are defined in the configuration file.
Rule files are listed in the configuration file.
Scrape intervals are configured in the config file, globally or per job.

explanation: Command-line flags configure immutable system parameters such as storage locations and retention. The config file defines scrape jobs, their instances, and which rule files to load.
hint: Which one is about the server's storage rather than what it scrapes?

stem: Which of these trigger a configuration reload in a running Prometheus? Select all that apply.

options.text: Sending SIGHUP to the Prometheus process
options.note: Right. SIGHUP triggers a reload.

options.text: An HTTP POST to /-/reload when --web.enable-lifecycle is enabled
options.note: Right. The lifecycle endpoint needs that flag.

options.text: Editing the file. Prometheus watches it and reloads automatically
options.note: Prometheus doesn't automatically reload prometheus.yml when it changes. You trigger a reload.
That's Prometheus's own metrics endpoint. It doesn't reload anything.

explanation: A configuration reload is triggered by sending SIGHUP to the process, or by an HTTP POST to /-/reload when --web.enable-lifecycle is enabled. Invalid configs aren't applied.
hint: One is a Unix signal, the other an HTTP endpoint behind a flag.

stem: You reload Prometheus with a config file containing a YAML error. What happens?

options.text: The new configuration isn't applied, and Prometheus keeps running with the previous one
options.note: Right. If the new config isn't well-formed, the changes aren't applied.
A bad reload doesn't take the server down. The changes are simply rejected.

options.text: Prometheus applies the valid parts and skips the rest
options.note: It's all or nothing. A malformed config isn't applied.
It keeps the last good configuration rather than resetting.

explanation: Prometheus can reload its configuration at runtime. If the new configuration isn't well-formed, the changes won't be applied.
hint: Prometheus is designed to stay up.

stem: A target exposes metrics at http://app:8080/metrics. Which scrape_config settings can you leave at their defaults? Select all that apply.

options.note: Right. It defaults to /metrics.
Right. It defaults to http.
job_name is required. Every scrape config names its job.
Prometheus can't guess the host and port. You list them, or discover them.

explanation: Defaults in scrape_config: metrics_path is /metrics and scheme is http. job_name and the targets must be provided.

stem: With the default honor_labels: false, a scraped series already has a job="batch" label, which conflicts with the job label Prometheus attaches. What happens?

options.text: The scraped label is renamed to exported_job and Prometheus's job label is attached
options.note: Right. Conflicting scraped labels become exported_<name>.

options.text: The scraped job="batch" label is kept and the server's value is ignored
options.note: That's what honor_labels: true does.
Conflicts are resolved, not treated as failures.

options.text: Both labels are kept under the same name
options.note: A series can't have two values for one label name.

explanation: With honor_labels false, conflicts are resolved by renaming the scraped labels to exported_<original-label> (such as exported_job) and then attaching the server-side labels. True keeps the scraped values, which is useful for federation and the Pushgateway.
hint: Look for the prefix Prometheus adds to the loser of a conflict.

stem: When is setting honor_labels: true typically useful?

options.text: When scraping the Pushgateway or in federation, where the target's own labels should be preserved
options.note: Right. The docs name exactly these two cases.

options.text: When you want Prometheus to ignore all target labels
options.note: The opposite. It preserves labels from the scraped data.
It's about resolving label conflicts, not performance.
TLS is configured with tls_config, unrelated to honor_labels.

explanation: Setting honor_labels to true is useful for federation and scraping the Pushgateway, where all labels specified in the target should be preserved.
hint: Where would the scraped job and instance labels be the meaningful ones?

stem: You want to stop storing one very expensive metric from a target while still scraping the target. Which section do you use?

options.text: metric_relabel_configs with a drop action on __name__
options.note: Right. Metric relabeling runs on scraped samples just before ingestion, so it can drop individual series.

options.text: relabel_configs with a drop action on __name__
options.note: Target relabeling runs before the scrape and acts on the target's labels. It can't see individual metrics.
Recording rules create new series. They don't stop existing ones being stored.
The timeout doesn't filter metrics.

explanation: Metric relabeling is applied to samples as the last step before ingestion. One use is excluding series that are too expensive to ingest. Target relabeling rewrites target labels before scraping.
hint: Which section runs after the samples have arrived?

stem: In a relabel config with action: keep and regex: web, which source label value would be kept?

options.note: Right. Relabel regexes are anchored at both ends, so only the exact value web matches.
The regex is anchored, so web doesn't match webserver. You'd need web.* for that.
Anchoring means the match must cover the whole value.
Anchoring rules that out. Use .*web.* to match anywhere.

explanation: Relabel regexes are RE2 and anchored on both ends. To un-anchor, use .*<regex>.*.

stem: Which relabel action drops targets whose concatenated source labels do NOT match the regex?

options.note: Right. keep retains only matching targets and drops the rest.
drop removes targets that do match.
labeldrop removes labels whose names match. It doesn't drop targets.
replace writes a value into target_label. It doesn't drop anything.

explanation: keep drops targets for which the regex doesn't match the concatenated source_labels. drop removes those that do match.
hint: Think of the name: what do you keep?

stem: After target relabeling finishes, what happens to labels whose names start with __ (such as __address__ or __meta_*)?

options.text: They're removed from the label set
options.note: Right. Double-underscore labels are dropped after relabeling. Copy any you need into a normal label first.
They're internal and removed after relabeling, so they don't end up on stored series.
exported_ renaming is part of honor_labels conflict handling, not this.

options.text: They cause the target to be dropped
options.note: They're just removed. The target is still scraped.

explanation: Labels starting with __ are removed from the label set after target relabeling. The instance label defaults to __address__ if it wasn't set during relabeling.
hint: Recall what the __ prefix means in the data model.

stem: If relabeling doesn't set the instance label, what value does it take?

options.note: Right. instance defaults to __address__.
The job name goes into the job label.

options.text: The hostname of the Prometheus server
options.note: instance identifies the target, not the scraper.
It's set from __address__ by default.

explanation: After relabeling, the instance label is set to the value of __address__ by default if it wasn't set during relabeling.
hint: Which special label holds the target's host and port?

stem: When are global external_labels attached to series or alerts?

options.text: When Prometheus communicates with external systems such as federation, remote storage or Alertmanager
options.note: Right. That's what external means here.

options.text: On every sample stored in the local TSDB
options.note: They aren't added to locally stored samples. They're applied when talking to external systems.
Grafana doesn't apply them. Prometheus does, towards external systems.
They're not specific to up.

explanation: external_labels are the labels to add to any time series or alerts when communicating with external systems: federation, remote storage and Alertmanager.
hint: The name tells you the audience.
